title: Chain clauses satisfied by the completed assignment
statement: Fix a clause index $i$ and a clause presented as a list of literals over a variable type $V$, and let $\alpha : V \to \mathrm{Prop}$ be an assignment that makes at least one literal of the clause true. Let $ml$ be a map lifting each literal over $V$ to a literal over the extended type $\mathtt{AuxVar}\,V$, and let $\alpha_3$ be an assignment on $\mathtt{AuxVar}\,V$ such that: (i) for every $k$ the auxiliary variable $y_{i,k}$ is true under $\alpha_3$ exactly when all of the first $k+2$ literals of the clause are false under $\alpha$; and (ii) for every literal $\ell$, the lifted literal $ml(\ell)$ is true under $\alpha_3$ if and only if $\ell$ is true under $\alpha$. Then for every chain counter $j \ge 1$, letting $\mathit{lits}$ be the suffix of the clause obtained by dropping its first $j+1$ literals, every 3-clause in the chain built for clause $i$ from $\mathit{lits}$ starting at counter $j$ is satisfied by $\alpha_3$.
hypotheses_covered: assignment α satisfies at least one literal of the clause
α₃ assigns each auxiliary variable y_{i,k} the value 'all first k+2 clause literals false under α'
ml preserves literal truth between α₃ and α
lits is the clause with its first j+1 literals dropped
replaced:
Let $\alpha$ be an assignment satisfying at least one literal of a clause, and let
$\alpha_3$ be an assignment on $\mathtt{AuxVar}\,V$ that evaluates auxiliary variables via
\texttt{SATTo3SAT.extraVal} and lifted literals faithfully.  Then every 3-clause produced
by $\texttt{SATTo3SAT.buildChain}\,c\_idx\,ml\,\mathit{lits}\,j$ (with $j \ge 1$ and
$\mathit{lits} = \mathit{clause}.\mathtt{drop}(j+1)$) is satisfied by $\alpha_3$.
